title: Regular pullback of internal Hom and strict-local testing
statement: Let $\ell$ be a prime, $r\geq1$, and $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^r\mathbf Z$. Schemes below are Noetherian excellent schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Use the bounded constructible small etale category $D^b_c$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] and, for $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$, $D_K=R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(-,K)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Write $\eta_M:M\to D_K^2M$ for the transpose of evaluation after symmetry of the tensor factors. Let $p:Y\to X$ be a regular morphism, meaning flat with geometrically regular fibres. For $L\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ and $Q\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ the evaluation-induced map $$p^*R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(L,Q)\longrightarrow R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(p^*L,p^*Q)$$ is an isomorphism. It respects evaluation and its transposes: if $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ and both $L$ and $D_KL$ lie in $D^b_c$, the two applications identify $p^*D_K^2L$ with $D_{p^*K}^2p^*L$ and $p^*\eta_L$ with $\eta_{p^*L}$. Pullback $p^*$ is exact and preserves bounded constructibility. In particular a strict localization $X_{(\bar x)}\to X$, the spectrum of the strict henselization of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], is a regular morphism with Noetherian excellent source of finite Krull dimension. A morphism of etale complexes on $X$ is an isomorphism if its pullbacks to all these strict localizations are isomorphisms. Krull dimension is the supremum of lengths of chains of irreducible closed subsets [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. For local rings, dimension equivalently uses chains of prime ideals [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. The potential pinnings of $p^*K$ are not part of this statement; they are lem-per-regular-pullback-pinnings.

source.place: Expose XVII, Proposition 4.2.2 (regular base change of internal Hom), Proposition 6.2.3.2 for the biduality identification, and the strict-local testing reduction at the beginning of 6.5

proof.text: Inverse image with transported constant coefficients is exact by [lem-trf-geometric-inverse-image-exact]. Thus its termwise action has $\mathcal H^n(p^*A)=p^*\mathcal H^n(A)$, since kernels, images and their quotients are preserved. It is triangulated by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. Pulling back a constructible sheaf preserves constructibility by [prop-constructible-pullback]; its finite module operations are transported by the same exact inverse image. Consequently pullback preserves the cohomological bounds and bounded constructibility. These assertions hold for every scheme morphism, with no regularity assumption.

source.place: Expose XVII, 4.2.2 and 6.2.3.2; exact constant-coefficient inverse image and constructibility

proof.text:
Write $H(A,B)=R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(A,B)$ and $\beta_{A,B}:p^*H(A,B)\to H(p^*A,p^*B)$. Use the tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] and the evaluation adjunction [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] to define $\beta$ as the unique transpose of $p^*\mathrm{ev}_{A,B}$. Hence
$$\mathrm{ev}_{p^*A,p^*B}\circ(\beta_{A,B}\otimes1)=p^*\mathrm{ev}_{A,B},$$
with the tensor comparison understood. This equation gives naturality in both variables by transposition. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction], internal Hom is triangulated in each variable and restricts to etale slices; the evaluation-defined comparison restricts to that same comparison because restriction takes evaluation to evaluation. The comparison is compatible with shifts in $A$: the tensor comparison and evaluation commute with the shift isomorphisms, with the sign of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction], so the transposes do too. Hence for a distinguished triangle $A'\to A\to A''\xrightarrow{\delta}A'[1]$ the three maps $\beta_{A'',B},\beta_{A,B},\beta_{A',B}$ form a morphism between the image triangles under $p^*H(-,B)$ and $H(p^*-,p^*B)$. The two squares over $A'\to A\to A''$ are naturality in the first variable; the connecting square is naturality for $\delta$ composed with the shift compatibility. Thus the assertion that $\beta$ is invertible is etale local and is closed under shifts and distinguished triangles in $A$, by [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso].

source.place: Expose XVII, Proposition 4.2.2, proof, printed pp. 281–282

proof.text: First suppose $A=M_X$ for a finite $\Lambda$-module $M$. The finite ring $\Lambda$ is Noetherian (it has finitely many ideals), so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-free-resolution-noetherian] supplies a resolution $P^\bullet\to M$ by finite free modules in degrees $\leq0$. Its constant sheaf complex is still a resolution: the constant-sheaf functor is a geometric inverse image and is exact by [lem-trf-geometric-inverse-image-exact]. Choose a bounded-below representative $N^\bullet$ of $B$ by [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative]. The ringed-site model [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-bounded-free-rhom-model] computes both $H(M_X,B)$ and $H(M_Y,p^*B)$ by the corresponding Hom complexes. If $N^j=0$ for $j<a$, their degree-$n$ terms use only $a-n\leq i\leq0$. Inverse image preserves this finite sum, and $\mathcal Hom(\Lambda^{r_i},N^{i+n})=(N^{i+n})^{r_i}$. Thus termwise pullback is an isomorphism of these Hom complexes, respecting $d_Nf-(-1)^nf d_P$. The map is $\beta_{M_X,B}$: its composite with evaluation is the pulled-back evaluation on each finite-free term. This proves the constant case without assuming that $M$ has finite projective dimension.

source.place: Expose XVII, Proposition 4.2.2, proof, printed pp. 281–282

proof.text: If $A$ is lisse, an etale covering makes it a finite constant module by [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. Over each member of that cover Step 3 applies, and Step 2 identifies its map with the restriction of $\beta_{A,B}$. The base-changed etale covering covers $Y$. Hence every geometric stalk of every cohomology sheaf of $\beta_{A,B}$ is invertible, and [lem-weil-pbc-derived-stalk-conservative] gives invertibility. This argument works for any morphism and any bounded-below $B$.

source.place: Expose XVII, Proposition 4.2.2, proof, printed pp. 281–282

proof.text: For the constructible-sheaf case we prove a stronger induction assertion: for every closed subscheme $T$ of $X$, every regular $v:W\to T$ between Noetherian schemes with $\ell$ invertible, every constructible sheaf $A$ on $T$, and every $B\in D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$, $\beta^v_{A,B}$ is invertible. Induct on the underlying closed subset using [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal]; the assertion is uniform in the scheme structure on that subset. The empty case is zero. For nonempty $T$, there is a dense open $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ on which $A$ is lisse: use its finite locally closed stratification [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] and the finitely many irreducible components [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components]. On each component its generic point's stratum contains an open neighborhood in that component; remove the other components and the closed complement of that neighborhood. The union of these finitely many disjoint component opens is a dense open on which $A$ is lisse: the stratum's immersion restricted over a component open $V$ is an immersion with the same image as the open immersion $V\hookrightarrow T$, and the restriction of a lisse sheaf to an open is lisse, so [lemma-constructible-immersion-independence] makes $A|_V$ lisse. Put $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ for the reduced closed complement. Restriction preserves constructibility by [prop-constructible-pullback]. The open schemes are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]; closed subschemes are Noetherian by the quotient case of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian].

source.place: Expose XVII, Proposition 4.2.2, proof, printed pp. 281–282

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-etale-internal-hom-localization] to $(A,B)$ on $T$, and to $(v^*A,v^*B)$ on $W$. By Step 1, pulling back the first triangle is still distinguished. Write $W_U=W\times_TU$, $W_Z=W\times_TZ$, with induced $v_U,v_Z$ and immersions $j',i'$. These are open and closed immersions by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. The maps $v_U,v_Z$ are regular: open restriction preserves the flatness and geometric fibre condition; for the closed restriction use the finite-type ring base-change theorem [lem-weil-pbc-regular-base-change] on affine charts. All schemes remain Noetherian; in particular $j$ and $i$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The right vertices of the two triangles are identified by [lem-per-regular-etale-direct-image-base-change] with $g=j$, followed by Step 4 on $U$. The left vertices are identified by that same theorem with $g=i$, followed by the induction assertion on the proper closed subset $Z$ with second argument $i^!B$, and then by [lem-per-regular-supported-base-change], which identifies $v_Z^*i^!B$ with $i'^!v^*B$. The supported functor takes $D^+$ into $D^+$ by its right-derived definition.

source.place: Expose XVII, Proposition 4.2.2, proof, printed pp. 281–282

proof.text: These left and right comparisons and the middle comparison $\beta^v_{A,B}$ form a morphism of the localization triangles in Step 6. Indeed, the arrows in [lem-per-etale-internal-hom-localization] are obtained from the open/closed extension triangle by internal adjunction. Transposing their comparison squares turns them into naturality squares for evaluation composed with the open restriction unit and closed supported counit. The defining evaluation equation in Step 2 gives the former equality. The latter is precisely the closed-counit compatibility in [lem-per-regular-supported-base-change]. Therefore the actual evaluation-induced $\beta$, rather than an arbitrarily chosen isomorphism of middle vertices, is the middle map. Since the outer maps are invertible, [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] makes it invertible. This completes the induction for constructible sheaves. For $L\in D^b_c$, the finitely many truncation triangles [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle] build $L$ from its shifted constructible cohomology sheaves. Step 2 and the same triangle criterion give $\beta_{L,Q}$ for all bounded-below $Q$.

source.place: Expose XVII, Proposition 4.2.2, proof, printed pp. 281–282

proof.text:
For the biduality clause put $D=H(-,K)$, $D'=H(-,p^*K)$ and $F=p^*$. Step 7 gives $b=\beta_{L,K}:FDL\xrightarrow{\sim}D'FL$ and $c=\beta_{DL,K}:FD^2L\xrightarrow{\sim}D'FDL$, using exactly the two assumed constructibility hypotheses. The identification of double duals is
$$a=D'(b^{-1})\circ c:FD^2L\xrightarrow{\sim}D'^2FL.$$
To compare the bidual arrows, transpose $a\circ F\eta_L$ under the evaluation adjunction [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal]. Precompose its transpose with $1_{FL}\otimes b$, an isomorphism. By the evaluation equation for $c$ and the definition of $\eta_L$, the resulting pairing is $F\mathrm{ev}_{L,K}\circ\sigma_{FL,FDL}$. The evaluation equation for $b$ makes this equal to $\mathrm{ev}_{FL,FK}\circ\sigma_{FL,D'FL}\circ(1\otimes b)$, the same precomposition of the transpose of $\eta_{FL}$. Cancel $1\otimes b$ and transpose back. Thus $a\circ F\eta_L=\eta_{FL}$. Pullback respects the symmetry here: on the signed tensor representatives both orders send a bidegree $(u,v)$ tensor to $(-1)^{uv}$ times the exchanged tensor. The tensor comparison is the representative comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. No pinnings or dualizing hypothesis on $K$ are used.

source.place: Expose XVII, Proposition 6.2.3.2, formal biduality identification, with general K and the two explicit constructibility hypotheses

proof.text: Fix an affine neighborhood $\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $x$, with $\mathfrak p\subset R$ the prime of $x$, and let $K$ be the separable closure of $\kappa(x)$ in the geometric point. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-ring-triples] the coordinate ring $C$ of $X_{(\bar x)}$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit] is canonically the colimit of the triples $(B,\mathfrak q,\phi)$ over $(R,\mathfrak p,K)$, compatibly with the maps from $R$. So by [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples] $C$ is a local filtered colimit of etale $R$-algebras, i.e. ind-etale over $R$. By [lem-exc-affine-strict-local-ring-comparison] there is an $R$-algebra isomorphism of $C$ with an algebraic strict henselization $(R_{\mathfrak p})^{\mathrm{sh}}$ of the local ring $R_{\mathfrak p}$ relative to $K$ [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization], compatibly with the structural maps to $X$. The pair category $(S,\chi:S\to K)$ of that definition for $(R_{\mathfrak p},K)$ is isomorphic to the triple category of [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples] for $(R_{\mathfrak p},\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p},K)$: $\chi$ has prime kernel $\mathfrak q$ over the maximal ideal and induces $\phi:\kappa(\mathfrak q)\to K$, and conversely $\chi=S\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)\xrightarrow{\phi}K$; morphism conditions agree. So $C$ is the strict henselization meant in [lem-sc-strict-henselization-noetherian]. The local ring $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian], so $C$ is Noetherian by [lem-sc-strict-henselization-noetherian]. Since an ind-etale map is weakly etale by [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability], and $R$ is excellent by the hypothesis on $X$, [lem-exc-weakly-etale-excellent] gives excellence of $C$. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-finite-krull-dimension] gives finite dimension of $C$, hence of its spectrum under the two dimension conventions in the statement.

source.place: Expose I, Theorem 8.1(iv) and its strict-henselization consequence, printed p. 16; Expose XVII, beginning of 6.5; Stacks Noetherian and local dimension inputs

proof.text: The map $R\to C$ of Step 9 is flat since it is weakly etale. To check geometric regularity of a fibre, base change it to any finite extension $k'$ of a residue field of $R$. Its algebra $B=C\otimes_R k'$ is weakly etale over $k'$ by [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability]. It is Noetherian: $C\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ is a localization of $C/\mathfrak qC$, and tensoring it with the finite extension is finite type, so use [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. By [lem-weil-pbc-weak-etale-field], $B$ is the union of finite etale $k'$-subalgebras. For $t\in B$ choose such an algebra containing $t$. Being a finite product of separable fields, it contains $u$ with $t=t^2u$. In any local ring $B_{\mathfrak b}$ this identity says that each nonzero element is invertible (the idempotent $tu$ is 0 or 1). Thus each such local ring is a field, of dimension zero and maximal ideal zero, and is regular by [def-weil-regular-scheme]. This proves the required geometric regularity. Hence $X_{(\bar x)}\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, and therefore its composite with the affine open immersion into $X$, is regular. This verifies that Steps 1–8 apply to strict localizations.

source.place: Expose I, paragraph before Theorem 8.1 (ind-etale implies absolutely flat implies regular), printed pp. 15–16; Expose XVII, beginning of 6.5

proof.text: Let $f:A\to B$ be a morphism of etale complexes whose pullbacks to all strict localizations are isomorphisms. At the closed geometric point of $X_{(\bar x)}$, the stalk of each pulled-back cohomology map is the original map $\mathcal H^n(f)_{\bar x}$: use exactness from Step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ]. Therefore every such stalk map is an isomorphism. For bounded-below complexes this gives the assertion directly by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-stalk-conservative]. For arbitrary complexes the same argument applies separately to each cohomology sheaf: [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] makes each $\mathcal H^n(f)$ invertible, so $f$ is a quasi-isomorphism, which is an isomorphism in the derived category by its definition [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Conversely an isomorphism remains an isomorphism under every pullback functor. No uniform dimension bound on $X$ is needed.
